title: Generated audio and job records expire on a retention policy
description:
Nothing in Auritus ever ages out. The jobs table is declared with
`time_to_live_attribute="ttl"` in `cdk/stacks/backend.py`, but the only writer
of a `ttl` attribute anywhere in the Lambdas is the alerts table -- job records
never get one, so the TTL configuration does nothing. The audio bucket is
created with no lifecycle rules at all. Every clip ever generated is stored
and billed forever.

That is a cost leak and a privacy liability: the jobs table holds the full
extracted text of every narrated page, indefinitely, with no expiry.

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Retention of generated audio and job records

  Scenario: A completed job is stamped with an expiry
    Given the retention period is ninety days
    When a job is marked done
    Then the job record carries an expiry ninety days in the future

  Scenario: Regenerating a job extends its expiry
    Given a job marked done sixty days ago
    When the operator forces regeneration and it completes
    Then the job expiry is ninety days from completion

  Scenario: Audio objects expire on the same schedule
    Given the retention period is ninety days
    Then the audio bucket expires objects after ninety days

  Scenario: Retention is configurable at deploy time
    Given the deployer sets the retention period to thirty days
    When the backend is deployed
    Then job records and audio objects both expire after thirty days

  Scenario: Retention can be disabled
    Given the deployer disables retention
    When a job is marked done
    Then the job record carries no expiry
```

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/stacks/backend.py`**

- Read `retention_days` from CDK context, defaulting alongside the existing
  `delivery_grace_seconds` / `fallback_seconds` constants. `0` disables.
- Add a lifecycle rule to `audio_bucket`:
  `s3.LifecycleRule(expiration=Duration.days(retention_days), enabled=retention_days > 0)`.
- Pass `RETENTION_DAYS` to the router Lambda's environment.

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`**

- `RETENTION_DAYS = int(os.environ.get("RETENTION_DAYS", "0"))`
- In `_mark_done` (and `_mark_failed`), when `RETENTION_DAYS > 0`, set
  `ttl = int(time.time()) + RETENTION_DAYS * 86400` on the update. The
  regenerate path clears the terminal attributes, so a regenerated job picks
  up a fresh `ttl` when it next completes -- verify that, do not assume it.

**Important:** the S3 lifecycle and the DynamoDB TTL must use the same
retention value, or audio outlives its record (an orphaned object nobody can
find) or a record outlives its audio (a `done` job whose signed URL 404s).
The second is worse; if they must drift, let audio expire last.

**`docs/`** — document the setting in the self-hosting guide. An operator
deploying Auritus needs to know their reader's page text is retained and for
how long.

## Open question for the architect

Ninety days is a placeholder. Retention interacts with the caching premise:
an expired job means the next reader re-triggers generation and pays for a
GPU again. A long retention is cheap in GPU and expensive in storage; a short
one inverts that. Audio is small and GPU is not, which argues for a long
default -- a year, or disabled by default with the mechanism available. Decide
before implementing.

comments.text: Implemented on feature/job-audio-retention, merged to develop. Retention defaults to DISABLED (retention_days=0) -- an explicit architect decision documented in code, consistent with this stack's existing RETAIN-everywhere posture, so no existing deployment silently starts losing data. A single retention_days variable threads both the S3 lifecycle rule on the audio bucket and the jobs table's ttl attribute (previously declared but completely inert), so they can never drift apart -- verified by a dedicated CDK test asserting the S3 expiration and the Lambda env var match, not just that both exist. _mark_failed also stamps ttl (a scope decision beyond the story's literal Gherkin, well-justified: the privacy concern is the extracted page text, which a failed job's record holds just as much as a done one's), which correctly required extending _retry_admin_job's REMOVE clause the same way auritus-9fcb40 extended _regenerate_admin_job's. Documents the DynamoDB TTL background-sweep caveat (~48h, not instant) and explicitly states the GPU-cost-vs-storage-cost tradeoff in docs/SELF_HOSTING.md, including that auritus deploy doesn't pass through --context and how to actually set this. Independently re-verified: reverted the fix myself and confirmed 2 of 3 scenarios genuinely fail (the disabled-by-default one is honestly reported as vacuous pre-fix, since there's no retention code path yet to break either way). Full suite green: black/ruff, cli pytest (75 passed), behave (31 features, 121 scenarios), cdk pytest (53 passed), cdk synth clean both with retention disabled and with retention_days=90. No fixes needed in review.
